description.short_caption: Blood smear showing extracellular spiral-shaped organisms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stained peripheral blood smear with numerous red blood cells and a few extracellular spiral-shaped organisms, consistent with spirochetes. The organisms are thin, elongated, and exhibit a helical morphology. The smear also includes occasional artifacts or debris. The stain highlights the spirochetes distinctly against the background of red blood cells.

Case_09013/figure1.jpg.source_caption: Wright stain of the peripheral blood.

description.short_caption: Wright stain of peripheral blood showing intracellular and extracellular findings.
description.detailed_description: This Wright-stained peripheral blood smear shows numerous red blood cells with a few white blood cells visible. A prominent finding is the presence of a thread-like organism, likely a microfilaria, seen extracellularly. The red blood cells appear normochromic and normocytic, and there is no significant rouleaux formation or hemolysis. The staining highlights cellular morphology and the presence of the parasite.
